tools.name: read_account
tools.description: The loan: type, repayment plan, balance and the current monthly payment.

tools.name: list_history
tools.description: The payment history by period since repayment began: from, to and status. Open one with read_history_entry by its 'from' month (YYYY-MM) for the detail.

tools.name: read_history_entry
tools.description: One period of the payment history in full, by its 'from' month (YYYY-MM): what was due, what was paid and when, and the kind of any deferment or forbearance.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a secure message to Loanbridge's customer service.
tools.says: Message sent. Loanbridge answers within 10 business days.

tools.name: list_employers
tools.description: The employers paying you through Payroll Harbor: name, EIN, start date, position and status.

tools.name: read_hours
tools.description: Average hours worked per week, by half-year, for one employer by name or for both.

tools.name: search_mail
tools.description: Search the mail; every word must appear in the sender, the subject or the message's labels. Omit the query for every message. Paged. Open one with read_message.

tools.name: read_message
tools.description: One message in full, by message id.

tools.name: read_rules
tools.description: The rule (34 CFR 685.219) as AidPath explains it, by topic: employers, full_time, contractors, payments, deferments, buyback, certification, reconsideration. Omit the topic for the index.

tools.name: read_tracker
tools.description: The forgiveness tracker: each period of the payment history with the months in it, the months counted and the reason a month was not counted.

tools.name: list_certifications
tools.description: Employment certifications already processed or pending.

tools.name: search_employers
tools.description: The PSLF employer database: search by EIN or by words of the name. Says whether the employer is a qualifying employer and why.

tools.name: submit_certification
tools.description: Send an employment certification form to an employer's official to sign: the EIN as the employer database shows it, the employer's name, the dates of employment being certified (YYYY-MM-DD; leave end_date empty if still employed) and the average hours per week.
tools.says: Certification for {employer_name} sent to the employer's official to sign.

tools.name: request_reconsideration
tools.description: Ask the Department to reconsider the count for one tracker period, by its period id, with the months you say should count and why.

tools.name: request_buyback
tools.description: Ask to buy back the months of one tracker period spent in a deferment or forbearance that does not count, by its period id.
tools.says: Buyback request received for {period_id}. You will be told the amount to pay.

phases.message: My PSLF count looks too low. Start here at Loanbridge: go through my loan and the whole payment history and note what happened in each period: payments, deferments, forbearance, anything late.
This is Payroll Harbor, where my two current jobs pay me. Note what you need about each employer and my hours.
Now my mail. Find every earlier employer and job in there, with dates, hours and how I was paid.
And this is AidPath. Certify every employer that counts, ask for reconsideration of any period that was miscounted, and tell me where my count stands after that.

rules.text: Topics: employers, full_time, contractors, payments, deferments, buyback, certification, reconsideration. Forgiveness follows 120 qualifying monthly payments on Direct Loans under a qualifying plan while working full time for a qualifying employer.

Qualifying employers: a government organization (federal, state, local or tribal, including school districts and public libraries), a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, or another nonprofit providing a qualifying public service. Not qualifying: a business organized for profit, a labor union, or a partisan political organization (685.219(b)).

Full time means an average of at least 30 hours a week during the period certified, in one or more qualifying jobs. Hours at two qualifying employers in the same period are added together; certify each employer with its own hours.
Only employees count. A worker paid as an independent contractor counts only where state law prevents the qualifying employer from employing someone in that role directly (685.219(b)).

A month counts when the full scheduled amount was paid under a qualifying plan (income-driven plans and the 10-year standard plan) while employed full time by a qualifying employer. A payment paid in full but late still counts: the rule that a payment be made within 15 days of the due date ended on July 1, 2023. Months of the COVID-19 payment pause (March 2020 to August 2023) count as if paid, for months of qualifying employment.

These months count when employment qualified (685.219(c)(2)): economic hardship deferment, cancer treatment, military service and post-active-duty deferments, AmeriCorps, National Guard and Department of Defense forbearances, and administrative and mandatory administrative forbearance. General (discretionary) forbearance does not count. The grace period does not count: no payment was due.

Months in a deferment or forbearance that does not count can be bought back, if employment qualified in those months, by paying what a qualifying plan would have required (685.219(g)(6)). A buyback is processed only if it results in forgiveness: the months bought back must complete the 120.

Certify each employer separately, with the dates and the average weekly hours to be certified; the employer's official signs. A processed certification is credited to every month it covers. Employment at a non-qualifying employer cannot be certified.

If the tracker did not count a month that the rule counts, ask for reconsideration of that period with the reason. Periods that wait only for an employment certification are counted once the certification is processed.
